content.comment_body: Hello! I have a sensor generating approximately 0–15 volts analog signal. I want to limit voltage over 10 volts using a serial resistor (multi-turn trimmer) to utilize the full scale of the sensor. Does anyone know the appropriate range for the trimmer—should it be 1 kOhm or 10 kOhm? I think I will find some answers through this approach :-) Best regards:
For a [product_name] base module [article_no], the analog input impedance according to the manual is 72 kOhm. I recommend using a 4.7 kOhm resistor in series with a 10 kOhm potentiometer.

Hello! I couldn't find the input impedance of [product_name] through web searches, so thank you for providing it :-) I will try using a 10 kOhm multi-turn resistor. The PCB has been designed so I can adjust the 'cut-off' voltage as needed. Best regards: [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user asked for the analog input impedance value to properly configure a voltage divider for a sensor connected to a [product_name] base module. It was challenging for them to find this technical specification online or in manuals. Another user shared the necessary impedance information and advised on resistor values, assisting with their decision.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated that documentation about the analog input impedance for the [company_name] [product_name] Basis Module would be readily available to help with their sensor hardware setup.
